options: a:Yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection, then proceed.,b:Proceed immediately without yielding.,c:Wait four seconds before moving.,d:Turn only if no vehicles are behind you.
note: A green arrow indicates you may go in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, how should you use the brakes?
options: a:Use the brakes lightly,b:Pump the brakes rapidly,c:Apply full force to the brakes,d:Do not use the brakes at all
note: After a blowout, slow gradually by lifting off the gas and using the brakes lightly; do not brake hard or jerk the wheel.

question: When driving on wet pavement you should remember:
options: a:Roads are especially slippery right after rain begins.,b:Hydroplaning can occur at high speeds.,c:Give yourself extra space when stopping.,d:All of the above.
note: Wet road surfaces are particularly slick shortly after rain starts; hydroplaning is a risk, and you should increase following distance and brake smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left you should:
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Swing to the right of your lane.,d:Accelerate slightly to make the turn faster.
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; only turn when the way is clear.

question: Which definition best matches distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving.,b:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,c:Only using a cellphone while driving.,d:Driving while tired only.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that diverts attention from driving—visual, manual, or cognitive distractions.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway you should:
options: a:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Follow closer to reduce wind effects.,c:Drive in the truck's blind spot to stay out of traffic.,d:Always pass on the right.
note: Trucks have larger blind spots and longer stopping distances, so leave extra following distance when behind them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You may not pass when a solid yellow line is on your side of the centerline; passing is allowed only when the broken line is on your side.

question: At a red light that displays a green arrow in your direction, you may proceed if:
options: a:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:You first come to a complete stop.,c:You wait for the circular green light.,d:You yield only to oncoming vehicles.
note: A green arrow indicates you may turn in the arrow's direction if you are in the proper lane. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection before turning.

question: If oncoming headlights blind you at night, what is the correct action?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes.,b:Switch to high beams to see better.,c:Look directly at the lights to get used to them.,d:Close your eyes briefly.
note: Glance to the right edge of the road rather than at the oncoming lights to keep your vehicle safely positioned until the vehicle passes.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Dangerous; always check carefully.,b:Safe to cross most of the time.,c:Safe places to park.,d:Only dangerous at night.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially hazardous. Look and listen for trains, obey signals and flaggers, and never cross until it is safe.

question: If your vehicle starts to lose traction due to water on the road (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid applying the brakes.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to stop immediately.,c:Drive at a constant higher speed to regain traction.
note: If hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator and slow gradually without braking hard, which can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: At a four-way stop you must yield to motorists who arrived before you.
options: a:True.,b:False.,c:Only if they signal.,d:Only if they are on the right.
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order of arrival; yield to those who arrived before you.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:A minor traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is a serious safety hazard; impairment endangers you and others on the road.

question: True or False: Drivers should avoid driving beside large vehicles for extended periods and be cautious when passing them.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots on both sides; it is safer to fall back or move ahead rather than remain alongside them for long.

question: When you see a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always come to a complete stop even if no children are present.,c:Sound your horn to clear children from the road.,d:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Pentagonal school signs warn of children crossing; slow down, watch for children, and be ready to stop.

question: What should you do when encountering a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,b:Stop, then enter when safe.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; slow down and be alert as you enter the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Only if you can see at least 200 feet in both directions.
note: If no stop line or crosswalk exists, stop at the nearest point where you can see oncoming traffic before entering the intersection; do not enter to get a better view.

question: An inattentive driver is one who:
options: a:Daydreams or stares off the roadway while driving.,b:Maintains eye contact with passengers constantly.,c:Only watches the vehicle directly ahead.,d:Uses mirrors regularly.
note: Distractions such as daydreaming, looking away from the road, or focusing on passengers reduce attention and increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds.,b:Night driving.,c:Slow speeds.,d:Driving in the rain with headlights on.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the severity of collisions due to greater energy at impact.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?
options: a:You may not proceed in the arrow's direction until it turns green,b:You may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic,c:You may turn after stopping completely,d:You may proceed with caution
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in the indicated direction until a green signal is shown.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic queues behind you on a two-lane road, what must you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed further,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass,c:Not allow other cars to pass you,d:Stop in the lane until traffic clears
note: If you are impeding traffic by driving significantly below the flow, pull over at a safe spot and let vehicles pass.

question: When passing a bicyclist you should:
options: a:Slow down and give the cyclist as much space as possible.,b:Drive into the bicycle lane until you can pass.,c:Honk to alert the bicyclist to move over.,d:Pass very quickly and close to the cyclist.
note: Bicyclists are vulnerable road users; slow down and allow as much lateral space as possible when passing.

question: Which statement about vehicle blind spots is correct?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger cars.,b:Blind spots disappear if you have only one outside mirror.,c:You can check blind spots using the inside rearview mirror.,d:Blind spots are not a safety concern.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, vehicles have blind spots you cannot see; large trucks have much larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.

question: At about what speed can cars begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:35 miles per hour,b:45 miles per hour,c:40 miles per hour
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds above about 35 mph depending on tire tread and water depth; reduce speed in standing water.

question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or carrying a white cane, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,b:Continue driving; pedestrians must yield.,c:Flash your headlights to alert them.,d:Honk to warn them to wait.
note: Blind or partially sighted pedestrians may use a cane or guide dog and must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: Faced with an oncoming car to the left and a bicyclist to the right, what is safest?
options: a:Let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist so you only handle one hazard at a time.,b:Split the difference and pass between them.,c:Pull onto the shoulder between the two hazards.,d:Attempt to pass both at once quickly.
note: When multiple hazards exist, handle them sequentially: wait for the oncoming car to pass, then pass the bicyclist safely.

question: Are you required to obey school crossing guards?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only when children are present.
note: You must obey the directions of crossing guards whenever they are directing traffic near schools.

question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:The speed at which you are traveling affects almost everything else that can happen to you in a car.,b:Heavy traffic situations do not affect safe speed.,c:It is always permissible to drive the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: Speed influences stopping distance, control, and crash severity; adjust speed for road, weather, and traffic conditions.

question: Should motorists keep a safe operating distance when near cyclists?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Drivers must be especially careful around bicyclists and maintain a safe following distance, usually at least three to four seconds.

question: Which types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Over-the-counter, prescription, and illegal drugs (all of the above).,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only prescriptions.
note: Many kinds of drugs—illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medicines—can impair driving ability and should be used with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is never fatal.,c:Speeding is not dangerous if you are skilled.
note: Both excessive speed and driving significantly slower than traffic can be hazardous; speeding increases the severity of crashes and slow driving can lead to hazardous passing maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only if the pedestrian waves to you.,c:Only if the pedestrian is not distracted.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks at all times; stop and yield to anyone already in the crosswalk or intersection.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign at a crossing,b:You have the right-of-way at all railroad crossings,c:You may pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is safe,d:You need not stop for a crossing without gates
note: Follow flagger instructions and stop signs at crossings; obey all crossing signals and signage.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited,d:You may cross to pass if no cars are coming
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate no passing from either direction.

question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Only the right lane may pass.,d:Passing allowed only during daylight.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no crossing to pass from either direction except to turn or under specific safe conditions.

question: When emergency vehicles are using sirens and flashing lights, what must drivers do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to them,b:Ignore them and continue driving,c:Follow closely behind them,d:Pull into the intersection and wait
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using audible and visual signals and follow any directions given by their operators.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:On a hill,b:In a parking lot,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane,d:In front of your driveway
note: Certain locations, such as crosswalks and marked bike lanes, are unlawful for parking and create hazards.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow when visibility is reduced, what should you do to help others see you?
options: a:Turn on your headlights,b:Use only your parking lights,c:Increase your instrument panel brightness,d:Flash your high beams
note: Use your headlights (low beams) whenever visibility is poor so others can see your vehicle.

question: What are "No zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where smaller cars disappear into the truck's blind spots.,b:Safe spaces to travel close behind the truck.,c:Areas where you can squeeze around while it turns.,d:Designated passenger loading zones.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots to the sides, rear, and front; avoid lingering in these "No zones" where you may be invisible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parked uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply away from the curb,b:Turn the wheels sharply toward the curb,c:Point the wheels straight ahead,d:Turn the wheels slightly to the right
note: Facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb so the back of the front tire rests against it and prevents rolling into traffic.

question: How should you respond to a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?
options: a:Stop if you can do so safely; a red arrow is coming,b:Proceed immediately without yielding,c:Merge into any lane shown by the arrow,d:Honk to alert other drivers
note: A steady yellow arrow warns the protected turning time is ending; stop if it is safe to do so.

question: If another car appears likely to hit you, what should you do first?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn the other driver.,b:Wave your arms out the window.,c:Use emergency lights only.
note: Use your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians in situations where they may not see you and a collision is imminent.

question: Which item is a common contributing factor to crashes?
options: a:Exceeding speed limits or driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.
note: Driving above posted limits or too fast for conditions is a major factor in crashes. Staying alert and scanning reduces risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?
options: a:Stop at the intersection and then proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow and drive through the intersection without stopping.,c:Turn right only.,d:Wait for a green light to appear.
note: A flashing red light means stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, what should you do?
options: a:Turn around and find another route; do not drive through flooded areas.,b:Slam on the brakes to avoid water.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,d:Try to drive through at low speed.
note: Never attempt to drive through flood water; even shallow water can hide hazards and may sweep your vehicle away.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:A construction zone ahead.,c:Passing is prohibited for both directions.,d:Bike lane separation.
note: A broken yellow centerline means drivers in either direction may pass when it is safe to do so.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest practice regarding speed?
options: a:Fluctuate your speed frequently to stay alert,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic,c:Drive slower than the flow of traffic,d:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limit
note: Driving with the flow of traffic at a safe speed (within posted limits) reduces crashes caused by speed differentials.

question: What is the safest way for small children to ride in a vehicle?
options: a:Secured in an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt for their size.,b:Held by a strong adult.,c:Standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
note: Children should always be properly restrained in an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt; holding a child during a crash is not safe.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are typically what color?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:White.,d:Orange.
note: Regulatory signs are usually white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green symbols or wording, and they indicate traffic laws that must be obeyed.

question: When you approach a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog who is crossing, you must:
options: a:Stop until the pedestrian is safely out of your path.,b:Carefully drive around them.,c:Sound your horn and proceed slowly.
note: When you encounter a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, you must stop and wait until the person is well clear of your path; always yield the right-of-way.

question: On a four-lane highway, if you approach a stopped school bus on the opposite side with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:You may continue driving; you are not required to stop when approaching from the opposite side.,b:Stop regardless of how many lanes there are.,c:Pass slowly while watching for children.
note: On highways with four or more lanes, vehicles traveling in the opposite direction of a stopped school bus are not required to stop, but should exercise caution near children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway you should be traveling:
options: a:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,b:Much slower than freeway traffic.,c:At the posted speed limit only.,d:At the speed recommended by signage only.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic to merge safely, provided that speed does not exceed the legal limit.

question: In a vehicle with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride?
options: a:In the front passenger seat.,b:In the back seat.,c:In the bed of a pickup truck.
note: Children age 12 and under should ride in the back seat to reduce risk from airbag deployment and crash forces.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, how should you prepare?
options: a:Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to clear the crossing quickly.,c:Drive around lowered gates if you don't see a train.
note: Approach railroad crossings cautiously: look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop when necessary.

question: When approaching the scene of an accident, what is the correct behavior?
options: a:Keep your attention on driving and keep moving unless you are involved or help is needed.,b:Stop and gather around to watch.,c:Drive to the scene to offer eyewitness accounts.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; keep driving and stay alert for people near the road.

question: Which of the following is true about passing a motorcycle?
options: a:You may pass a motorcycle without changing lanes partially,b:You do not need to be fully in the adjacent lane to pass,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle,d:Motorcycles must share lane markings so you can pass closely
note: Motorcycles occupy a full lane; drivers must move completely into the left lane when passing a motorcycle from the left.

question: A diamond-shaped roadway sign indicates what type of message?
options: a:Warning about a road hazard or special condition ahead.,b:An interstate route marker.,c:A school crossing only.,d:A regulatory command you must follow.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are generally warning signs indicating hazards or special roadway conditions ahead.

question: If your wheels drop off the roadway or pavement edge, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and wait until safe, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately and sharply.,c:Stop and call for help.
note: If your wheels leave the pavement, reduce speed, check traffic, and when safe, gradually steer back onto the roadway; do not jerk the wheel.

question: What common mistake do drivers make when backing up?
options: a:Failing to turn their head and look both ways out the rear window,b:Relying solely on rearview mirrors,c:Backing up slowly,d:Signaling too early
note: Many drivers fail to look over their shoulder and through the rear window; mirrors alone do not show everything.

question: True or false: If traffic is moving across a railroad track in a stream, it is safe to stop on the track briefly.
options: a:False.,b:True.,c:Only if no train is visible.,d:Only in an emergency.
note: It is illegal and unsafe to stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Never enter unless there is room for your entire vehicle on the far side.

question: Why are roads especially slippery just after rain begins, and what should you do?
options: a:Roads are slippery and you should slow down and avoid fast turns or stops.,b:Test tire traction while going uphill.,c:Decrease how far ahead you look.,d:Increase your speed to avoid puddles.
note: Oil and grime on the road combined with water reduce traction; slow down and avoid sudden steering or braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit in a rural area unless a higher limit is allowed by federal law?
options: a:60 mph,b:55 mph,c:40 mph,d:50 mph
note: In rural areas the maximum speed limit is 55 miles per hour unless federal law allows a higher limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians who cross against a traffic signal?
options: a:False — drivers should still yield when safe to do so.,b:True — pedestrians walking against a signal have no claim to right-of-way.,c:Only on highways.,d:Only at marked crosswalks.
note: Drivers should yield the right-of-way to pedestrians whenever necessary to avoid a collision, even if the pedestrian is not legally entitled to it.

question: Combining drugs with alcohol:
options: a:Increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:Lessens alcohol's effects.,c:Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,d:Only impacts long trips.
note: Mixing alcohol with drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) can increase impairment and the likelihood of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles carefully.,b:Sound your horn continuously while passing.,c:Flash your headlights as a signal to pass.,d:Pass without checking mirrors if the road looks clear.
note: Ensure you have enough distance to pass safely and that oncoming traffic is not approaching before changing lanes.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
options: a:Directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,b:Flashing red signals and gates are operating.,c:The crossing is controlled by a stop sign.,d:All of the above.
note: Stop when directed by flaggers or signs and whenever flashing red signals, gates, or audible warnings indicate an approaching train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive at a speed greater than which of the following?
options: a:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.,b:The posted maximum speed only.,c:A speed that is safe for the conditions only.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for road, weather, traffic, and visibility conditions while staying within legal limits.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what is the correct initial reaction?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop,b:Slam on the brakes immediately,c:Speed up to reach a safe area,d:Jump out of the car
note: If a tire blows, keep a firm grip on the wheel, steer straight, slowly reduce speed, and pull off the roadway when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:As soon as you clear the front bumper of the vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: How should you behave when another vehicle is passing you?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed and allow them to pass.,b:Brake hard to prevent them from passing.,c:Speed up to keep your position.,d:Honk continuously to warn them off.
note: When being passed, do not increase speed; hold a constant speed to allow the other vehicle to pass safely.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a moving railroad crossing gate?
options: a:If you first look carefully in both directions.,b:If an approaching train is not too close.,c:Never; do not drive around or under a lowering or lowered gate.
note: Never go around or under crossing gates that are moving or lowered; wait until lights stop and gates are fully raised.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.,d:A hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs the nervous system, slowing reaction time and dulling judgment.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby,b:Drive faster than the train to beat it across,c:Drive around any lowered gates,d:Ignore it if you do not see tracks
note: Railroad warning signs mean a train may be approaching; slow and be ready to stop. Never go around barriers.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossings.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: A crossbuck (X-shaped) sign marks a railroad crossing; yield to trains and obey any warning devices.

question: Is it wise to continually improve your driving and observation skills?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Because driving always involves risk, continuously improving driving and observation skills increases safety for you and others.

question: Is parking in a handicap access aisle beside a handicap stall permitted?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking in handicap access aisles is prohibited; these aisles provide space for wheelchair access and lifts.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Release your seat belt,b:Brace against the seat back and put your head against the head restraint,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly,d:Be ready to apply the brakes if necessary
note: If hit from behind, do not release your seat belt; brace yourself against the seat and head restraint to reduce whiplash.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Judgment.,b:Vision.,c:Balance.,d:Hearing.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, then affects vision, balance, and coordination.

question: What does the acronym BAC stand for?
options: a:Blood alcohol consent,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC),c:Base alcohol content,d:Body alcohol content
note: BAC (blood alcohol concentration) measures the percentage of alcohol in a person's blood and indicates impairment level.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you stop at an intersection because of a signal?
options: a:When you see a flashing red light.,b:When you see a steady yellow light.,c:When you see a yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop like a stop sign; proceed only when safe after stopping.

question: When exiting the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed to a safe level before entering the curve.,b:Brake sharply while in the curve.,c:Maintain freeway speed until halfway down the ramp.,d:Shift to neutral before the curve.
note: Slow to a safe speed before entering a curve on a ramp; braking in the curve can cause a skid.

question: Why should you leave extra space in front of a large truck?
options: a:Because trucks take longer to stop and need extra room to stop safely.,b:So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.,c:So other drivers have room to slow down in front of the truck.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances than cars. Avoid pulling in front of a truck then slowing to reduce crash risk.

question: What is true about tailgating (following too closely)?
options: a:It can anger other drivers and may result in legal consequences.,b:It cannot lead to a traffic citation.,c:It reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.,d:Is encouraged on busy roads.
note: Tailgating increases the chance of collisions and contributes to aggressive driving; it can also lead to citations.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address securely attached to the parked vehicle.,b:Wait indefinitely for the owner to return.,c:Call your insurance only after you get home.
note: If you strike a parked vehicle or other property and cannot locate the owner, leave a note with your contact information affixed to the vehicle and report as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While you are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, you should:
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Pull to the left and stop.,d:Speed up and clear the intersection quickly.
note: If you are already in the intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, continue through, then move to the right and stop to let it pass.

question: If your vehicle has airbags, what should you also do for maximum protection?
options: a:Rely on the airbags alone.,b:Always wear your seat belt in combination with airbags.,c:Wear the lap belt behind your back.
note: Airbags are supplemental; lap and shoulder seat belts must be worn to provide the best protection in a crash.

question: Why is driving at night generally more difficult than driving during the day?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:It is more likely to rain at night.,c:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: Night driving reduces your field of vision; use appropriate headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

question: Which road marking or device is commonly used on some highways to indicate which lanes are for turning?
options: a:Arrows painted on the roadway and lane-use markings.,b:Flashing red lights on the shoulder.,c:White lines on the side of the road.
note: Arrows and lane markings on the pavement direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning.

question: True or False: Ramps and bridges tend to freeze before the main road surface.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only during heavy snow,d:Only in shaded areas
note: Bridges and ramps are exposed to air on all sides and can ice over more quickly than the roadway; use extra caution.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should you behave?
options: a:Watch closely for children and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop regardless of circumstances.,c:Sound your horn to warn children.,d:Drive faster to clear the area quickly.
note: Slow and be alert for children at school crossings; yield to pedestrians and be ready to stop.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, you should:
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.,d:Use neither if the airbags are present.
note: Wear both lap and shoulder belts for the best protection; using only one part greatly reduces effectiveness.

question: If you observe other drivers acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Don’t make eye contact and avoid gestures,b:React with hand gestures to show displeasure,c:Distance yourself from the situation and get away safely,d:Challenge them to change behavior
note: Mentally and physically distance yourself from aggressive drivers, avoid eye contact and provocative gestures, and move away when safe.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Make sure the pedestrian sees you before proceeding rapidly.,d:Honk to warn the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk; stop and let them cross safely.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:To warn others of an immediate danger, such as a child about to run into the street.,b:Every time you pass another vehicle.,c:When traveling through an intersection.,d:To express frustration at another driver.
note: Use the horn as a warning to alert others of imminent danger—not as a tool for expressing anger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight,c:Flash your headlights to get other drivers to yield,d:Turn wheels sharply to the right
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision won't push you into oncoming traffic.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A school zone or school crossing.,b:A stop requirement.,c:A regulatory command.,d:A general warning of hazards.
note: A five-sided (pentagon) sign is used to warn drivers that they are entering a school zone or school crossing area where children may be present.

question: What information do blue road signs provide?
options: a:Motorist services such as food, rest areas, and hospitals.,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:Mileage and distance to locations.
note: Blue signs indicate services available to motorists like hospitals, rest stops, and gas stations.

question: What color are guide (destination) signs that show directions and mileage?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green,d:Blue
note: Guide signs have a green background and provide direction and distance information to destinations.

question: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because others may try risky passes.,b:Recommended when you are unsure of the limit.,c:Always safer than driving at the flow of traffic.,d:Only acceptable in bad weather.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can frustrate other drivers and lead to dangerous passing maneuvers; try to travel with the flow within the legal limit.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light.,d:Increase speed to clear the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to slow, check for cross traffic, and proceed with caution when safe.

question: When should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:When weather reduces visibility so others can see you.,b:Only during heavy rainstorms.,c:To warn others of bad weather without using wipers.,d:It is not required to use headlights in rain.
note: If weather requires windshield wipers, you must also use low-beam headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you face a green traffic light but pedestrians are in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the green light.,c:Signal and continue through the intersection.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection; yield when turning on a steady green signal.

question: What is true about driving on wet roadways?
options: a:As speed increases, tires become less effective at removing water and may hydroplane.,b:Good tires eliminate all wet-road risks.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,d:Water improves tire traction at high speeds.
note: Higher speeds reduce tire ability to clear water, increasing the chance of hydroplaning; drive slower in wet conditions.

question: Which statements about steering are true?
options: a:Hands should be on opposite outside rim positions and use one hand only for backing or controls.,b:Always steer with one hand while driving.,c:Keep your thumbs inside the rim at all times.,d:Both of the above are incorrect.
note: Steer with hands on opposite outside rims (thumbs up); use one hand only when backing or operating a control that requires reach.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive and use alternatives such as taxis.,b:Just say “No thanks, I’m driving” after you start drinking.,c:Drink only beer so it is safer.,d:Wait five minutes before driving after stopping drinking.
note: The only reliable way to avoid drunk driving is to plan ahead not to drive if you will be drinking and arrange a sober ride.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive as close to the right edge of the road as possible and stop, avoiding stopping in an intersection.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,c:Stop immediately wherever you are, even in an intersection.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop, taking care not to stop in an intersection.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red,d:Blue
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: When parallel parking, the recommended approach is to:
options: a:Signal right, pull even with the car ahead, stop, then back into the space.,b:Drive into the space forward and back up as needed.,c:Stop 5 feet from the curb and maneuver in.,d:Park without signaling to avoid confusing others.
note: When parallel parking, signal, pull up even with the vehicle ahead of the space, and back in, parking within 18 inches of the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what three actions are important?
options: a:Signal your intentions, check your blind spot, and make sure the lane is clear.,b:Only signal and change lanes quickly.,c:Check mirrors after you have moved into the lane.
note: Before changing lanes always signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the target lane is clear.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Speed up before entering curves and brake in the curve.,c:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill only.,d:Test your tires by braking sharply while turning.
note: Slow before entering curves; braking in a curve may cause skidding on slippery roads.

question: What should you do before starting a parked vehicle?
options: a:Adjust the seat and mirrors and fasten your safety belt.,b:Check the fuel gauge and adjust the radio volume.,c:Adjust the side mirror and make sure the heater works.
note: Before starting, set your seat and mirrors for safe visibility and fasten your lap and shoulder belt.

question: When you see an approaching emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Maintain your speed and lane until it passes.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly.,d:Speed up to clear the way.
note: If an emergency vehicle approaches using lights, pull to the right edge and stop until it has passed.

question: Which statement about tires is correct?
options: a:Tires must have good tread and be free of damage,b:Under-inflated tires provide a smoother ride,c:Over-inflated tires do not skid on wet roads,d:Tires do not need regular inspection
note: Your tires must be in good condition with adequate tread and free from damage; inspect them regularly.

question: If you've had several beers, which action will actually reduce the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Drink several cups of coffee.,b:Wait several hours.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol; coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not speed this process. It takes about one hour to process one standard drink.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign represent?
options: a:The maximum legal driving speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a recommended safe speed.,c:The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket in all conditions.,d:A minimum speed requirement.
note: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions; you must slow down when conditions are less than ideal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you never do when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Move into another lane while inside an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes while inside an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It is illegal to turn off your signal early,b:It lets other road users know your intentions,c:It is unsafe to signal before a turn,d:It forces others to yield to you
note: Continuous signaling informs drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians of your intended movements, improving safety.

question: Which traffic control device corresponds to coming to a full stop, yielding to others, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A steady red arrow.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to others, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Demand the other vehicle yield to you.,d:Drive onto the shoulder at all costs.
note: On narrow roads, both drivers should leave adequate space; you must allow the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main-traveled portion so both can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin reducing speed as you prepare to exit an interstate?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,d:Only after reaching the exit ramp.
note: Maintain your freeway speed until you enter the deceleration lane; then reduce your speed to the posted advisory speed for the exit ramp.

question: True or False: Large trucks can have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE,c:Only on highways,d:Only when heavily loaded
note: Large vehicles have large blind spots, including directly behind them, so avoid following too closely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:Expect oncoming traffic to yield to you,c:Turn without yielding if you have a signal,d:Begin your turn as soon as the light turns green
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: Sudden gusts of wind on highways can:
options: a:Cause problems for all vehicles.,b:Only affect large vehicles.,c:Only reduce visibility.,d:Only affect motorcycles.
note: Strong winds can move or destabilize vehicles of any size and can also reduce visibility by blowing dust or debris into the roadway.

question: Warning signs that indicate upcoming hazards typically use which color scheme?
options: a:White letters on blue.,b:Black symbols on yellow.,c:Black symbols on white.,d:Red letters on yellow.
note: Warning signs use black symbols or lettering on a yellow background to alert drivers to upcoming hazards; work zones use orange.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight road with 500 feet clear view both ways.,d:At intersections with stop signs.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians.

question: When is it legal to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:If the warning lights are not flashing.,c:If you can see clearly both directions.
note: Do not go around or under any lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Wait until the gates are fully raised and lights/bells have stopped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or without signaling.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Avoid sudden or unannounced lane changes; always signal and check mirrors and blind spots first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While merging onto an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the flow of traffic at a matching speed.,b:Always stop on the ramp before entering.,c:Merge across two lanes at once to reach your destination faster.,d:Enter slowly and expect traffic to yield.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the freeway speed and merge into a safe gap, yielding to traffic already on the highway.

question: An orange and red triangular sign on the rear of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:A slow-moving vehicle.,c:Shoulder work ahead.,d:The vehicle is oversized.
note: An orange and red triangle denotes a slow-moving vehicle such as farm equipment or maintenance vehicles.

question: Why is it beneficial to look far ahead while driving on the highway?
options: a:It helps you keep up with traffic,b:It reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning,c:It allows you to spot upcoming police officers,d:It lets you text safely
note: Scanning far ahead gives you time to react, reducing sudden braking or swerving and improving overall safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The car ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: a:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have cleared.,b:Change lanes and cautiously pass the stopped vehicle.,c:Pass the vehicle slowly at 10 mph or less.,d:Sound your horn and pass on the left.
note: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; there may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance must you signal before turning according to South Carolina law?
options: a:100 feet.,b:50 feet.,c:150 feet.
note: South Carolina law requires signaling at least 100 feet before beginning any turn.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what assumption should you make?
options: a:Assume the driver may open a door into traffic and exercise caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Expect the parked vehicle to re-enter traffic immediately.
note: Allow extra space and be prepared for doors opening or the vehicle suddenly pulling into traffic.

question: If heavy smoke covers the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,b:Turn on high beam headlights and continue slowly.,c:Stop in the travel lane until smoke clears.,d:Increase speed to clear the area quickly.
note: If smoke limits visibility, slow down, pull as far right as possible, and stop safely off the road. Some smoke can be toxic and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you complete the turn?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane.,b:The rightmost lane.,c:Either lane at your discretion.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the lane closest to the one you came from; do not swing into other lanes.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to do which of the following?
options: a:Stop at the stop line,b:Stop before entering any crosswalk,c:Stop before entering the intersection,d:All of the above
note: A red light means stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk, and before entering the intersection unless directed otherwise.

question: When is highway pavement especially slippery?
options: a:Just after it begins to rain.,b:After it has been raining several hours.,c:One to two hours into a rain.,d:Only during heavy rainstorms.
note: Pavement is most treacherous when rain first begins because oil and dirt on the road mix with the rainwater and create a slick film.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When completing a pass, how will you know you have enough space to return to your lane?
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:The other driver signals you to return.,c:You can hear the passed vehicle honk.,d:You have waited at least five seconds.
note: Return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s front (both headlights) in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: Is it illegal to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must never attempt to share a single lane with a motorcyclist. Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane width.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Switch to high beams to see better.,c:Stare directly into the headlights.,d:Flash your lights repeatedly.
note: To avoid being blinded, glance toward the right edge of the roadway and follow that line until the oncoming vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you near an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Be prepared to stop safely; do not speed up to beat the red.,b:Accelerate to beat the light.,c:Stop abruptly in the center of the intersection.,d:Turn off your headlights.
note: A steady yellow means the light will soon be red; slow and stop if it is safe rather than speeding up to cross.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and stay in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, pull over to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: You only need to signal 50 to 75 feet before turning at an intersection in South Carolina.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only when other vehicles are present,d:Only at night
note: In South Carolina you must signal for at least 100 feet before making a turn.

question: What is true about excessive speed?
options: a:It often leads to high-risk decision-making and increases crash risk.,b:It reduces the chance of a crash.,c:It increases your ability to react to hazards.,d:It is always acceptable if you are an experienced driver.
note: Excessive speed is a leading factor in crashes; it reduces reaction time and promotes risky decisions.

question: What is the best way to handle being tailgated?
options: a:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass,b:Slam on your brakes to make them back off,c:Speed up to get away from the tailgater,d:Yell and gesture to the other driver
note: To reduce rear-end collision risk, move out of the lane if possible or slow gradually to let the tailgater pass.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic you should:
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely.,b:Flash your headlights and speed up to retaliate.,c:Pull alongside and yell at them.,d:Attempt to block their vehicle.
note: Avoid road rage and dangerous responses; let it go and maintain safe driving behavior.

question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
options: a:Loss of hearing.,b:Increased fuel economy.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.,d:Brake failure.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment, which is toxic and potentially deadly.

question: Which drivers are covered by the South Carolina Point System?
options: a:Only permit holders.,b:Only intermediate drivers.,c:All licensed drivers.,d:Only drivers with prior convictions.
note: All drivers are subject to the South Carolina Point System; accumulation of points for violations can lead to suspension of driving privileges.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Left foot for braking and right for accelerating,b:Right foot for both braking and accelerating,c:Either foot for braking,d:Alternate feet to improve reaction time
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake to maintain consistent and safe pedal control.

question: At night, which of these is most difficult to see?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.,d:Traffic lights.
note: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night compared to road signs or other motorists, so be extra cautious and use headlights properly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane street, what must be true before you can pass safely?
options: a:You can see the road ahead clearly and can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:Your vehicle is capable of the speed to pass, regardless of visibility.,c:You have signaled for at least 50 feet.,d:Other drivers wave you on to pass.
note: You may only pass when you have clear visibility, can return before oncoming traffic, and it is legal and safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs tell you?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed allowed on that roadway under ideal conditions,b:Suggested safe speeds only for bad weather,c:Recommended speeds for heavy traffic,d:How fast other drivers are traveling
note: Speed limit signs indicate the legal maximum (or minimum) speed under ideal conditions; adjust for weather and road conditions.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:It helps keep traffic flowing faster.
note: Leaving space around your vehicle provides time to react to sudden stops, errors by other drivers, and road hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what is the first maneuver you should make?
options: a:Pull up even with the car ahead of the space you want,b:Turn the wheel to the right immediately,c:Back in at full speed,d:Stop in the middle of the lane
note: After signaling and checking traffic, stop parallel to the vehicle in front of your chosen space before backing in.

question: True or false: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not significantly increase your crash risk.
options: a:False.,b:True.,c:Only true for hands-free phones.,d:Only true when driving slowly.
note: Using a phone while driving distracts attention and significantly increases crash risk.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:Only if another vehicle yields first.,d:Only if the emergency vehicle is behind you.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights by pulling over and stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never — you always have the right-of-way.,b:Whenever yielding helps prevent a collision.,c:Only at uncontrolled intersections.
note: Always yield when doing so prevents a crash. Right-of-way should be given to avoid collisions, even if you technically have it.

question: How can you help the driver behind you keep a safe following distance?
options: a:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintain a steady speed and signal early for maneuvers.
note: Maintain a steady speed and give early signals to help the driver behind judge a safe following distance.

question: Is holding a driver license a right or a privilege?
options: a:A right,b:A privilege,c:A requirement,d:A guarantee
note: Driving is a privilege that must be earned and maintained; it is not an absolute right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Proceed through the intersection with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns you to slow down and proceed with caution after yielding to any crossing traffic or pedestrians.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Do not use high beams in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility. Use low beams instead.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and vehicle speeds are harder to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are always fewer vehicles on the road at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes judging distance and speed difficult; you can only see as far as your headlights allow.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is not permitted.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,c:A center turn lane is present.,d:A pedestrian-only zone.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; a solid white line means lane changes and passing are discouraged or prohibited.

question: What must you do when a school bus is stopped ahead with lights flashing and its stop arm extended?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Change lanes and pass slowly.,c:Stop only if children are in the road.,d:Proceed if you are in the opposite lane of a divided highway.
note: When a school bus is stopped loading or unloading with flashing lights and stop arm extended, stop and remain stopped until it is withdrawn and safe.

question: For drivers under 21, at what BAC can the license be suspended?
options: a:Any detectable amount of alcohol.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:0.15 percent or more.
note: South Carolina has zero tolerance for drivers under 21; any detected alcohol can result in penalties, including license suspension.

question: What do yellow lines on the roadway separate?
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Carpool lanes from regular lanes.,d:Bike lanes from vehicle lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads and separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:When exiting an expressway only.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance when a large vehicle blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or if being tailgated.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Allow additional following distance from the vehicle ahead,b:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear,c:Approach other vehicles with extra caution,d:All of the above
note: In sleet or snow, keep windows clear, increase following distance, and drive cautiously to allow extra stopping time.

question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:They need longer distances to stop due to their size and weight.,b:Truck drivers can always stop quickly.,c:Because large vehicles travel slower than passenger cars.,d:Small vehicles are easier to see behind trucks.
note: Large vehicles require much longer distances to stop; sudden stops in front of them can lead to rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.
note: Signal both when pulling toward a curb and when pulling away from it so other road users know your intentions.

question: What should you do on slippery roads?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive faster to get through the area quickly.,c:Always drive at the posted limit even if conditions are poor.,d:Brake sharply to test traction.
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet to maintain traction and control.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,b:Only illegal drugs impair your driving.,c:Prescription drugs are always safe if you feel alert.,d:No drugs affect driving if taken in small amounts.
note: Prescription and OTC medications can affect driving ability; it is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate.,b:Never pass them under any circumstances.,c:Flash your lights to make them aware of you.,d:Drive as close as possible to their rear bumper.
note: Avoid lingering beside large vehicles and keep a safe distance to escape their large blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what should you do?
options: a:Always slow down in your current lane.,b:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.
note: Always check mirrors and then look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: Which of the following is a common cause of crashes?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots,c:Always yielding the right-of-way,d:Using seat belts properly
note: A frequent cause of collisions is driving at speeds that are unsafe for the current road or weather conditions.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, what should you do?
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.,b:Leave vehicles in the traffic lane until police arrive.,c:Immediately drive away from the scene.,d:Walk away from the vehicles and leave them.
note: If no injuries and you can do so safely, move vehicles out of travel lanes to prevent further collisions and clear traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn through the median to reach your exit.,b:Stop and back up to your exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and re-route safely.
note: If you miss an exit, do not stop or back up on the highway; proceed to the next exit and find a safe route back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout, to whom should you yield?
options: a:Any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists as well as traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Only vehicles inside the roundabout.,c:Only to cars, not pedestrians.
note: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the entry, and yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is prohibited for both directions.,c:Passing on the right is required.,d:The road is one-way.
note: A broken yellow centerline allows drivers to cross the centerline to pass if no oncoming traffic is present and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action is prohibited when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.,b:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Do not cross the centerline in an intersection to change lanes. Always ensure the lane is clear before moving over.

question: When another driver is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position while being on guard and allow space if they need to return to your lane.,b:Speed up to prevent them passing.,c:Move out of the lane immediately regardless of conditions.
note: When being passed, maintain speed and position, be on guard for unsafe actions by the other driver, and allow space if they need to merge back.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:More dangerous due to reduced visibility and other factors.,b:Less dangerous.,c:No different.,d:Safe if you use high beams always.
note: Night driving is more hazardous because it is harder to see, and glare or impaired drivers may be present.

question: On a four-lane roadway, must you stop for a stopped school bus when you are traveling in the opposite direction?
options: a:True (you do not need to stop when traveling opposite on a divided four-lane),b:False
note: On a highway with four or more lanes, vehicles traveling in the opposite direction of a stopped school bus are not required to stop, though exercise caution near children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what is your required action?
options: a:Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Always stop before proceeding no matter what.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: Slow or stop if needed and yield the right-of-way to any cross traffic close enough to be a hazard.

question: At a railroad crossing, what must you be sure to do?
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings and be cautious of multiple trains.,b:Only look for trains coming from one direction.,c:Rely on crossing gates alone to indicate a train is coming.
note: Approach railroad crossings with extreme caution, watch for vehicles that must stop at all crossings (school buses, hazmat trucks), and ensure no trains are coming from either direction before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection blocked by traffic ahead, you should:
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can clear it.,b:Move forward slowly to keep traffic flowing.,c:Get as close to the car ahead as possible.,d:Enter the intersection and wait.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it; blocking an intersection is illegal and dangerous.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.,b:No passing is allowed from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted only on the right.,d:Both directions may pass freely.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, drivers beside the broken line may pass when safe; those beside the solid line may not.

question: When changing lanes, how can drivers see objects in their blind spots?
options: a:Look over the left or right shoulder toward the blind spot.,b:Trust the outside mirror only.,c:Use the inside rearview mirror only.,d:Flash headlights to make other vehicles visible.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen with mirrors alone. Look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to check blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle in the same direction, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,b:After about three seconds,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle behind you,d:Immediately after passing
note: Do not return to your lane until you can clearly see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:The green arrow protection is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.,b:You should speed up to make the turn before the light changes.,c:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning time is ending; yield to oncoming traffic and prepare to stop.

question: What following distance should you maintain under normal driving conditions?
options: a:At least a three- to four-second gap.,b:One-second gap.,c:Following distance is only important on snow and ice.
note: Under normal conditions keep at least a three- to four-second following distance; increase it for adverse weather, higher speeds, or heavy traffic.

question: When must headlights be used?
options: a:From a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise,b:Only after 7 p.m. and before 7 a.m.,c:Only during heavy rain,d:When parking on the shoulder
note: Headlights are required from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced.

question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Passing is prohibited for both directions.,d:It marks a bike lane.
note: A dashed yellow centerline separates opposite-direction traffic and indicates passing is allowed when safe.

question: If you suffer a tire blowout while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid braking until the vehicle has slowed.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly to stop immediately.,c:Tap or pump the brakes to slow down.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the accelerator to slow gradually and do not apply the brakes hard until the vehicle is slowed and under control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the normal flow of traffic, what may be required?
options: a:Pull off the road and let other vehicles pass if you are causing traffic to back up.,b:You always retain the right-of-way.,c:You should refuse to let others pass.
note: Driving far slower than traffic can be hazardous; on two-lane roads if you impede traffic you may be required to pull off and allow vehicles to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?
options: a:Proceed to the next exit and find a safe route to your destination.,b:Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder.
note: Never back up on a freeway or shoulder; continue to the next exit and safely re-route.

question: If dust or smoke reduces your visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers.,b:Turn on parking lights only.,c:Slow down and turn on your headlights.
note: When visibility is reduced, slow down and use headlights so other drivers can see you; pull off if you cannot see safely.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Pedestrian crossing.,c:Merging traffic.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if it is safe to do so.,b:Always remain at your present speed regardless of traffic.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.
note: On multi-lane roadways, move over one lane if it is safe and there is no adjacent traffic, to allow merging vehicles to enter safely.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error,b:New drivers,c:Bad weather,d:Mechanical failure
note: Most collisions result from human error—drivers failing to see others or making unexpected mistakes.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes, at any time,b:No, except to turn into a driveway or private road,c:Yes, if no oncoming traffic is present,d:Only if you signal first
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross only to turn into a driveway or entrance where allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statements about driving speed are true?
options: a:Higher speeds increase the chance of fatality and you should increase following distance at higher speeds.,b:Speed has no impact on fatality risk.,c:Faster speeds always reduce stopping distance.,d:Speed has no effect on stopping distance.
note: As speed increases, collision severity and fatality risk rise, and stopping distance increases so you should leave more space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you travel relative to conditions and other vehicles?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions and within the posted limit.,b:Always at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:Always at the speed of surrounding vehicles no matter what.,d:At the maximum possible speed for your vehicle.
note: The speed you choose should be appropriate for conditions and legal limits; reduce speed when conditions are poor.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Get out of the car and go for help,b:Lay down in your car and go to sleep,c:Walk into the road to flag down drivers,d:Stay in your car and wait for help, making yourself visible
note: Staying in your vehicle keeps you sheltered and makes it easier for rescuers to locate you; conserve fuel and signal for help.

question: What can occur if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or OTC medicine?
options: a:The combination can multiply the impairing effects of alcohol or the medicine.,b:The medicine always blocks alcohol's effects.,c:Alcohol helps medicines work better.,d:No interaction occurs.
note: Alcohol combined with medications can increase impairment and be more dangerous than either alone.

question: When operating near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Avoid driving beside it for long periods.,b:Follow closely to reduce wind drag.,c:Drive on its right side on hills and curves.,d:Always pass immediately.
note: Large commercial vehicles have extensive blind spots on each side. Avoid driving alongside them for long stretches where the driver cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Never; do not pass on the shoulder.,b:When the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Only if the shoulder is wide enough.,d:If traffic is stopped ahead.
note: Passing on the shoulder is prohibited because other drivers do not expect vehicles there and may change direction into it.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or during an equipment check, what must a driver produce if requested?
options: a:Proof of registration.,b:Proof of insurance.,c:Their driver license.
note: When stopped for a traffic violation or an equipment inspection, a driver must be able to present their driver license, and should have proof of vehicle registration and proof of insurance available in the vehicle.

question: If an aggressive driver is tailgating you, you should:
options: a:Make every effort to get out of their way.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Speed up to increase the gap.,d:Brake-check them.
note: Avoid confrontation and safely move out of the aggressive driver's way; do not engage or escalate the situation.

question: After an accident you should:
options: a:Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured.,b:Report the accident the following week.,c:Leave the scene and call your insurance company from home.,d:Only exchange insurance information if requested.
note: Stop, protect the scene if possible, call law enforcement, render aid if trained, exchange information, and report as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian?
options: a:To any pedestrian crossing a street in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,b:Only to pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,c:Only when pedestrians signal you to stop.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks; for safety, yield to people crossing any street when appropriate.

question: When driving in fog, is using your high beam headlights recommended?
options: a:True,b:False
note: High beams should not be used in fog because the light will reflect back and reduce your visibility; use low beams instead.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic does instead.,c:Assume the guard's directions are optional.
