note: Obey crossing guards' directions; they ensure the safety of pedestrians and schoolchildren.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should the maximum posted speed limit be driven?
options: a:Only at night,b:Only during the day,c:Only under ideal driving conditions,d:Whenever traffic is heavy
note: Posted maximum speeds apply to ideal conditions; you must reduce speed when conditions are less than perfect.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Whenever another vehicle is in your way.,b:When it may help prevent a collision.,c:To express annoyance at a slow driver.
note: Only use the horn to warn others of danger or to avoid a collision; do not use it to express frustration.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Stay alert, slow down, obey signs and flaggers, and be prepared to react to hazards.,b:Activate your four-way flashers and continue at the same speed.,c:Increase your speed to avoid impeding traffic.
note: When entering a work zone, slow down, pay close attention, obey posted signs and flaggers, and be ready to respond to changing conditions or hazards.

question: Approaching an octagonal sign means you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Slow and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield only to oncoming traffic.,d:Turn left.
note: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a full stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when safe.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle using its siren or lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to a stop in your lane and wave it on.,b:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it first then stop.

question: Which method checks a blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,b:Use the inside rearview mirror only.,c:Use only the side mirror.,d:Sound your horn.
note: There are blind spots that mirrors cannot show; look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to verify it is clear.

question: Which statement about a work zone is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be stationary or moving and are marked with orange signs; drivers must slow down.,b:They are marked with black and white signs.,c:Drivers do not need to slow down in work zones.
note: Work zones can be stationary or mobile (e.g., mowing, line painting), are marked with orange signs, and require drivers to slow down and pay attention.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Blue,d:Red
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white marks separate same-direction lanes.

question: When a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended, drivers should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk to warn children before passing on the left.,c:Proceed when they think children have finished crossing.
note: You must stop for a school bus that is displaying its stop arm and lights and only proceed once the bus resumes motion and the arm is withdrawn.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:If stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.,b:Only if you are in an accident.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must have proof of financial responsibility (insurance) while driving and present it to an officer when requested after a traffic stop or collision.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing and see no train, when must you still stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If the crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.
note: Stop whenever indicated by a stop sign, lowered gate, flashing lights, or flagger; never assume it's safe without checking.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, what is the safest action?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn,b:Try to squeeze between the vehicle and the curb,c:Quickly turn before the truck completes its turn,d:Pass on the right between the truck and curb
note: Large vehicles need more space to turn; do not try to pass or squeeze between them and the curb—wait until the turn is finished.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels to the right toward the curb.,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels to the left toward the center of the road.
note: When parking downhill, turn the front wheels toward the side of the road so if the vehicle rolls it moves away from traffic.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:You are changing lanes,b:Your emergency brake is on,c:You are making a turn,d:You are slowing down or stopping
note: Brake lights indicate you are slowing or stopping and must be in working order to warn following drivers.

question: Which behavior is a common sign of impaired (drunk) driving?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving consistently with traffic flow.,c:Using turn signals properly.
note: Signs of impairment include weaving, swerving, sudden braking, driving too slowly or too fast, and jerking motions.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips on the road?
options: a:Through sound and vibration they warn inattentive drivers that their vehicle is leaving the travel lane.,b:They help test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.
note: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to alert drivers that they are straying from the lane or approaching a hazard.

question: Drivers are prohibited from passing a school bus when its red lights are flashing:
options: a:True.,b:False.,c:Only on two-lane roads.,d:Only during school hours.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and the stop arm is out, all drivers must stop until the lights are turned off and the bus moves on.

question: Before driving while taking medication, what should you do?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about possible driving effects,b:Have someone follow you home,c:Leave your windows open while driving,d:Take an extra dose to stay alert
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving; ask a healthcare professional about effects before driving.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but has no lights or siren on, how should you respond?
options: a:Continue driving normally.,b:Stop immediately as quickly as possible.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to clear a path; continue normally.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is important.,d:Using snow tires can improve traction.
note: You should not use cruise control on snow, in rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions; winter driving requires extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the road center has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, you may:
options: a:Pass if traffic ahead is clear.,b:Pass only in an emergency.,c:Never pass under any condition.,d:Pass only during daylight hours.
note: If the broken line is next to your lane you may cross and pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: How would you describe backing (reversing) a vehicle?
options: a:Always dangerous because it's hard to see behind the vehicle.,b:Dangerous only in large vehicles.,c:Dangerous only when you have a helper.
note: Backing up is always risky due to limited rear visibility; use extra caution, helpers, or cameras when available.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct sequence when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder into your blind spot, then change lanes.,b:Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes immediately.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, then change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs traffic to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Follow the officer's directions and go through the intersection.,b:Obey the red light and stop until it turns green.,c:Refuse and wait for the light to change.
note: Directions from a police officer controlling traffic override traffic signals and signs; follow the officer's instructions.

question: If you must drive in fog, you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Only parking lights.,d:Interior dome lights.
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility even more.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you and another vehicle arrive at the same time and the other vehicle is on your right. What should you do?
options: a:Increase speed and hurry through the intersection.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right and wait.,c:Enter the intersection forcing the other vehicle to stop.
note: When vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right; allow it to proceed first.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement, what is the correct recovery technique?
options: a:Grip the wheel, slow by easing off the accelerator, then steer slowly back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Hit the brakes hard and jerk the steering wheel back onto the road.,c:Immediately swerve back onto the pavement at speed.,d:Stop in place and wait for help.
note: If wheels leave the pavement, hold the wheel, slow down gradually, and carefully steer back onto the road once it is safe.

question: At a railroad crossing that has only a crossbuck and no gates or lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming,b:Turn up your radio to better hear approaching trains,c:Cross quickly without stopping,d:Only proceed if another driver waves you on
note: Cross only after checking both directions and confirming no trains are approaching; obey any flagger instructions if present.

question: Which statement about backing on a roadway is correct?
options: a:Drivers should look behind them and check traffic before and while backing.,b:Drivers should look straight ahead while backing.,c:Traffic checks are not necessary when backing.,d:Only use mirrors when backing.
note: Always look over your shoulder and check behind your vehicle before and during backing to ensure the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following about left turns is correct?
options: a:Complete a left turn into the legal lane nearest your previous lane.,b:Swing wide into the right lane while turning left.,c:Always finish a left turn onto a four-lane roadway in the far right lane.
note: When turning left, you should complete the turn into the legal lane nearest to your previous lane; left turns on red are allowed only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both alertness and coordination.,d:None of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness, coordination, reaction time, and the ability to concentrate—skills essential for safe driving.

question: You must exercise extreme caution and yield to children playing in the street:
options: a:True.,b:False.,c:Only near schools.,d:Only if signs are posted.
note: Slow down and be especially alert in areas where children may be present such as neighborhoods, playgrounds, and near schools.

question: Regarding speed control in curves, what is most important?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed entering the curve and then slow at the sharpest part.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Increase speed before entering the curve to maintain momentum.
note: Slow down before entering a curve so your vehicle's inertia doesn't carry you too fast through the bend.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop from 55 mph?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:400 feet
note: Large tractor-trailers need much longer stopping distances than passenger cars; a fully loaded truck may need up to about 400 feet at 55 mph.

question: How should you adjust your driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Slow down because you have less traction than on pavement,b:Drive at the same speed as on pavement,c:Expect better visibility than on pavement,d:Brake hard in turns for better control
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and increase stopping distance; reduce speed and drive cautiously on gravel or dirt.

question: If you are involved in a collision, what should you do first?
options: a:Remain near the scene, move your vehicle to the shoulder if possible, and provide aid,b:Report the accident to the police within one week,c:Leave the scene and call your insurance company,d:Drive to the nearest service station
note: Stop, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, offer aid, notify police, exchange information, and file required reports.

question: What effect does even a small amount of alcohol have on driving abilities?
options: a:Even the smallest amount can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,b:Only levels above the legal limit have any effect.,c:Alcohol improves alertness.,d:Alcohol affects only balance, not judgment.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair attention, perception, judgment, and memory; no amount is safe for driving.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:You may not pass from your direction of travel.,b:Slow down immediately.,c:You may pass with caution.,d:The lane is for buses only.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates passing is prohibited from your direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, you should first:
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors and signal about 100 feet before changing lanes.,b:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.,c:Rely only on your mirrors and avoid turning your head.,d:Start signaling only after you begin the lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors for traffic, signal early (about 100 feet in residential areas), and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

question: Is it unlawful for a car to try to share a lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane. A car must not try to share a lane with a motorcycle.

question: When parking uphill on a roadway with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the side of the road (right).,b:Keep them straight ahead.,c:Turn them toward the center of the road (left).
note: On an uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road's edge so a rollback will not move into traffic.

question: If you are being tailgated and cannot change lanes, what is the correct response?
options: a:Wait until the way ahead is clear and then gradually reduce speed to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Brake sharply to scare the tailgater off.,c:Speed up to put distance between you.,d:Immediately pull to the left shoulder and stop.
note: If you can't move over, slow gradually when safe so the tailgater can pass; never brake abruptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing another vehicle in any marked no-passing zone or over a railroad crossing.,b:Passing only when it is safe.,c:Passing on multi-lane highways when lanes permit.
note: It is illegal to pass where signs or markings prohibit it, at railroad crossings, on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead, or when a solid yellow line is on your side.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop behind the gates and wait until they are raised and it is safe to proceed.,b:Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.,c:Slowly go around the gates if traffic is heavy.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when gates are lowered or warning signals indicate a train; driving around lowered gates is illegal and dangerous.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?
options: a:Neither direction may pass.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.,d:Only trucks may pass.
note: Double solid yellow markings indicate passing is prohibited from both directions.

question: When entering your parked vehicle you should:
options: a:Look around for obstacles or hazards before entering.,b:Enter only from the passenger side.,c:Signal traffic to stop so you can open your door.,d:Open the trunk first.
note: Before getting into your vehicle, walk around it and check for obstacles, children, or other hazards that could interfere with safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Check mirrors, signal early, and glance over your shoulder for blind spots.,b:Rely entirely on your mirrors.,c:Signal only after starting the lane change.,d:Signal at least 500 feet before residential lane changes.
note: Before changing lanes, check side and rearview mirrors, signal early (about 100 feet in residential areas), then glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

question: True or false: Work zones on highways have become increasingly safe for workers and drivers.
options: a:False.,b:True.,c:Only on rural highways.,d:Only under police supervision.
note: Work zones remain hazardous for workers and drivers; reduce speed and be attentive whenever you enter them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is approaching while you plan a three-point turnabout, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to all approaching traffic before starting the turnabout,b:Flash your headlights and start immediately,c:Begin the turnabout quickly to beat the traffic,d:Signal and proceed without checking for traffic
note: A three-point turn must only be made when it is safe; yield to all oncoming traffic before performing the maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement is true about driving too slowly?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:Speed does not affect safety.,d:It is always safer to drive slower than traffic.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic can create hazards as other drivers may attempt risky passing maneuvers.

question: The term 'No zone' refers to:
options: a:Blind spots around a truck or bus.,b:A special reduced-speed area.,c:A roadway with restricted radio volume.,d:A designated no-parking zone.
note: Large trucks and buses have blind areas on each side, in front, and in the rear where smaller vehicles may disappear from view; these are called 'no zones.'

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what is the best practice?
options: a:Plan your trip in advance,b:Depend only on road signs while driving,c:Only have a vague idea of your destination,d:Start driving and look up directions on the road
note: Before traveling to an unfamiliar area, review maps or directions and plan your route to reduce distractions while driving.

question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires with good tread and proper inflation, and reduce speed in rain.,b:Use high beams in the rain.,c:Drive faster over puddles to clear water.,d:Shift into neutral when entering water.
note: Good tire tread, correct inflation, and lower speeds in wet conditions reduce the chance of hydroplaning.

question: What is the penalty for refusing a chemical test when requested by law enforcement in South Carolina?
options: a:One month.,b:Three months.,c:Six months.
note: Under South Carolina's implied consent law, refusal to submit to chemical testing results in a six-month license suspension, in addition to other penalties.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for hazards?
options: a:Continuously scan the road and roadsides rather than staring straight ahead.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake when scanning.,d:Focus only on the vehicle directly ahead.
note: Search far ahead and scan the entire roadway and sides to identify hazards early and prepare to react.

question: If a vehicle is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass,b:Speed up to increase distance between you and the tailgater,c:Brake sharply to frighten them away,d:Stop in your lane until they pass
note: If you cannot change lanes, gently reduce speed to encourage the vehicle behind you to pass when safe.

question: As you approach the crest of a hill, what is the best precaution?
options: a:Speed up slightly to clear the hill.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain the same speed you had earlier.
note: Because you cannot see potential hazards over the top, reduce speed so you can stop if needed.

question: Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Change lanes away from it, or slow below the speed limit if you cannot change lanes.,b:Drive to the right and stop in the lane next to it.,c:Maintain speed and pass closely.,d:Speed up to get past the scene quickly.
note: If an emergency or roadside assistance vehicle is stopped with lights flashing, change lanes away; if unsafe, slow to below the posted speed and give space.

question: On average, how fast does the body eliminate alcohol?
options: a:About one standard drink per hour.,b:Two drinks per hour.,c:Three drinks per hour.
note: On average, the body processes roughly one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors affect this rate.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights at night, where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:Toward the center of the roadway.,c:Look straight ahead at the lights.
note: If an oncoming vehicle does not dim its lights, avert your gaze toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while maintaining lane position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway marked with double solid yellow lines, which action is allowed?
options: a:You may not cross them under any circumstance.,b:You may cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,c:You may cross them to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing in both directions; you may cross them only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on the roadway?
options: a:They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate passing may be allowed.,b:They separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:They mark pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Broken yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate that passing is permitted when safe.

question: Drowsiness while driving can have effects similar to what other impairments?
options: a:It can impair your judgment similar to alcohol and drugs.,b:It makes you a better, more alert driver.,c:It has no effect on driving ability.
note: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a four-lane highway, slower traffic should use which lane?
options: a:The left lane.,b:The right lane.,c:The center lane.,d:Any lane as long as you signal.
note: Slower-moving traffic should travel in the right lane; use left lanes primarily for passing.

question: What does a yellow diamond-shaped sign with black symbols typically indicate?
options: a:A warning about conditions on or near the road ahead,b:Directions to nearby cities and towns,c:Traffic laws and regulations,d:Maximum speed limits
note: Diamond-shaped yellow signs with black symbols are warning signs that alert you to road or traffic conditions ahead.

question: What does a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line mean about passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the solid line side.,b:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid line.,c:Passing is prohibited from either direction.
note: A solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line means vehicles on the broken-line side may pass when safe; vehicles on the solid-line side may not.

question: An octagonal road sign always means what?
options: a:Stop.,b:Speed limit.,c:Hospital ahead.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign is always a stop sign; you must come to a complete stop at a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind while going uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit and passing may be unsafe.,b:You will always be able to safely pass the truck.,c:The truck must always pull over to let you pass.,d:The truck will always be at posted speed.
note: Large vehicles often slow on inclines; on hills or curves with limited visibility, passing may be unsafe or unlawful.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:When changing lanes, turning left or right, or pulling toward/away from a curb.,b:Only when parking.,c:Only when passing another vehicle.
note: Always glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes, merging, turning, or pulling toward/away from a curb.

question: What is the correct top-to-bottom order of traffic lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Green, yellow, red.,c:Red, green, yellow.
note: From top to bottom traffic signals are red, yellow, green. Recognize this order when approaching intersections.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Cycling at night is more hazardous because bicycles are harder to see; both drivers and bicyclists should be extra cautious after dark.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you allow the motorcyclist to use?
options: a:A complete lane (full lane width).,b:Only half of a lane.,c:The shoulder beside the lane.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles and must be allowed a full lane width for safe maneuvering.

question: In fog, rain, or snow, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: A solid red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:The same as a circular red light; do not turn in the arrow's direction.,b:Drivers may proceed with caution.,c:The arrow is only advisory.,d:You may turn if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: A solid red arrow means traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.

question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body?
options: a:Time.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Drinking caffeine.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; food, caffeine, or other methods do not speed up BAC reduction.

question: True or False: Your driving speed has no effect on the distance your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE,c:Only on dry roads,d:Only with ABS brakes
note: Higher speeds require more distance to stop; speed directly affects stopping distance.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:A person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane,b:Other drivers and pedestrians will always observe the right-of-way,c:Driving closely to parked vehicles to allow more room for traffic,d:Assume parked cars will stay stationary
note: People or vehicles can unexpectedly emerge from between parked cars; leave space and be ready to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection mean?
options: a:You may drive through the intersection if the way is clear and may turn unless prohibited, yielding to others.,b:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.,d:Only pedestrians may proceed.
note: A steady green allows through movement or turns (unless posted otherwise) after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Another driver is attempting to pass your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road,b:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing,d:Speed up to prevent them from passing
note: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed or position so the passing vehicle can return to the lane safely.

question: What do pentagonal road signs indicate?
options: a:School zones and school crossings.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: A five-sided (pentagonal) sign marks school zones or school crossings; exercise extra caution near them.

question: Traffic signs with an orange background typically warn of:
options: a:Construction and maintenance work.,b:General roadway hazards.,c:Regulatory rules.,d:School zones.
note: Orange signs are used specifically for construction and maintenance warning messages.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light indicates drivers should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for green.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow signal means do not stop but slow down and proceed carefully after checking for hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from multilane, one-way streets?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The middle of the intersection.,c:The left lane.
note: To turn left from a one-way or multilane roadway, start from the leftmost lane designated for left turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from a ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and enter when it feels safe.,b:Check for traffic, reduce to 25 mph, then merge.,c:Check traffic, accelerate to match the flow, and merge when clear.
note: Use the acceleration lane to increase speed to match traffic on the interstate and merge safely when there is a gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Whenever a police officer orders you to stop,b:At a red traffic light,c:Both of the above,d:Only when there is a stop sign
note: You must obey officers directing traffic and come to a complete stop at steady or flashing red lights.

question: Before driving after taking medication, what should you do?
options: a:Understand the medication's effects and adjust your driving.,b:Drive immediately so the medicine won't affect you.,c:Make more rest stops than usual.,d:Double your following distance only at night.
note: Many medications can impair driving ability. Know the side effects and avoid driving if the medication affects your alertness, coordination, or judgment.

question: When sharing the road with bicyclists, you should do which of the following?
options: a:Treat bicycles as vehicles on the road and be extra careful when near them.,b:Pass as closely as possible because they're small.,c:Expect them to always yield to you.
note: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities. Be careful around cyclists, maintain a safe distance, and leave ample room when turning after passing.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line indicates what?
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass anytime.,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.
note: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means drivers on the side with the broken line may pass when it is safe to do so.
